papers.title: Simple Stacking Ensemble Machine Learning Approach for Vickers Hardness Prediction of Arc Vacuum Melted High-Entropy Alloys
papers.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) show excellent mechanical properties, but their enormous compositional space makes experimental and computational exploration expensive. This study predicts the Vickers hardness (HV) of HEAs from nominal elemental compositions (at.%) using a composition-based stacking ensemble machine learning approach without the use of handcrafted descriptors. A dataset of 120 vacuum arc-melted (VAM) HEAs containing 15 constituent elements (Re, Ru, Al, Si, Ti, Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta, and W) was compiled. Four baseline models, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector regression (SVR), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), and artificial neural networks (ANN), were evaluated. SVR achieves the highest baseline performance (R2 = 0.90). Stacking ensembles with the SVR meta-learner improved the weaker base learner performance by 17.20% and 12.50% for KNN-SVR and ANN-SVR respectively, relative to their base models. The best-performing stacking ensemble, XGB-SVR, only results in a minimal improvement of 2.90% compared to SVR. Ru, Re, and Al as the strongest positive contributors to hardness, as well as Fe, Co, and Ni as the strongest negative contributors, are identified with an interpretability test using permutation feature importance (PFI) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Validation on the held-out compositions showed prediction errors below 7%. This study indicates that the composition-only models could form the basis for an effective and interpretable approach for rapid HEAs hardness screening. However, the investigated stacking strategy offers limited benefit compared to the best-performing baseline model.

papers.title: Layer–Island Mixed Growth and Non-Equilibrium Structural Evolution of Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Al High-Entropy Alloy Thin Films: Insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulation
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used to study the deposition and growth of Fe-Co-Ni-M-Al multi-component alloy films on a Si(100) substrate. By comparing the surface topography at incident energies of 0.1~0.5 eV, it was observed that an increase in incident energy enhances local impact perturbations and induces surface roughening, with the film’s root-mean-square (RMS) roughness increasing from 0.3393 nm to 0.4870 nm. The selection of input data was consistent with the preparation conditions of the electron beam evaporation deposition process. The 0.1 eV condition, which yielded the best surface quality, was selected to study the deposition and growth process. The results indicate that deposited atoms first form a continuous covering layer on the substrate surface, followed by localized accumulation and island-like thickening, exhibiting characteristics of a mixed layer–island growth pattern. The radial distribution function (RDF) exhibits a stable first-neighbor peak at approximately 2.5 Å, with higher-order peaks and shoulders gradually appearing during the deposition process, indicating that short-range order formed within the film and gradually evolved into medium-range order. Polyhedral template matching (PTM) results show that the film exhibits a non-equilibrium structure characterized by a predominance of FCC structure, accompanied by the coexistence of HCP, BCC, and amorphous structures. Based on the solute formation rules derived from the atomic size difference δ and Ω parameter, as well as the empirical criteria of VEC, this composition exhibits the potential to form a solid solution and a structure with a tendency toward FCC. Meanwhile, both Debye-simulated XRD results and experimental data show a broadened main peak near 44°, cross-sectional SEM characterization confirms that the film surface is not completely flat but exhibits some local topographical variations, and TEM characterization reveals the presence of nanocrystalline/polycrystalline structures within the film; together, these findings demonstrate the ability of the MD model to predict the average atomic spacing and primary local order characteristics of the experimental film.

papers.title: Treatment of Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: from Radical Surgery to Perioperative Immunotherapy and Molecular Personalization
papers.abstract: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) is one of the most aggressive urologic malignancies and is characterized by a high risk of recurrence and progression even after radical surgical treatment. In recent years, approaches to MIBC treatment have undergone significant transformation due to the emergence of compelling data on the benefits of perioperative immunotherapy, the development of antibody-drug conjugates, refinements in organ-preserving strategies, and the introduction of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) as a potential molecular stratification tool. Recent scientific data demonstrate a shift from the predominantly anatomically-based "neoadjuvant chemotherapy → radical cystectomy" model to a perioperative system in which the choice of treatment intensity is gradually linked to tumor biology, the likelihood of response, tolerability of therapy, and the presence of molecular markers of minimal residual disease. ctDNA is gaining particular importance, potentially allowing for the differentiation of patients with high and low risk of recurrence after surgery. At the same time, a new concept of bladder preservation is emerging in carefully selected patients with a significant response to systemic treatment.

papers.title: Device-Specific Conformal Reliability under Scanner-Level Acquisition Shift in Breast Ultrasound CAD
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction provides finite-sample coverage control under exchangeability, but empirical reliability may change across scanner-defined deployment domains. We audit three conformal procedures and one non-conformal abstention baseline on leave-one-device-out (LODO) partitions of BUS-BRA using EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-50 and ConvNeXt-Tiny. All conformal thresholds are computed by direct finite-sample order-statistic indexing. The primary prediction and score unit is the image; source splits are patient-disjoint, target calibration/test partitions are patient-disjoint within each recalibration draw, and patient-cluster bootstrap plus patient-aggregated analyses assess within-patient dependence. At nominal α=0.05, EfficientNet-B0 Mondrian CP gives malignant set-miss rates of 0.004 for GE Logiq 7, 0.002 for GE Logiq 5 and 0.244 for Toshiba; the Toshiba patient-cluster 95% interval is 0.140-0.359. Patient aggregation preserves the contrast (0.194 for Toshiba versus 0.000 for both GE devices). In paired target recalibration, k=10 lowers Toshiba mean miss rate from 0.246 to 0.057 while increasing abstention to 0.603, whereas the same intervention raises the GE means to 0.060 and 0.067. Across the 500 Toshiba k=10 seed-draw combinations, the post-recalibration median miss rate is 0.021 (IQR 0.000-0.063), and 96.4% of draws improve relative to their paired pre-recalibration value. A finite-resolution analysis shows that α=0.02 is rank-unavailable for all tested few-shot conditions; under direct finite-sample order-statistic indexing, α=0.02 and α=0.05 coincide at k=5 and k=10 because both select the observed class maxima, but they separate in the larger k=20 condition. These results document scanner-level differences in empirical conformal reliability and motivate evaluating target recalibration when an independent target-domain reliability audit provides evidence of undercoverage, rather than establishing a prospective trigger rule.
